text:
Alyssa: seeing a weird pattern on eu-west1-rack8, inference tail latency spiking + a couple of GPU evictions over the last hour. not sure if it's thermal or power related
Matt: can you paste the node id and a quick nvidia-smi output?
Alyssa: node=gpu-eu-west1-rack8-12, attaching snippet:
```
Tue Mar 18 09:12:10 nvidia-smi
GPU 0: Temp=92C Pwr:75W/250W EnforcedPwr:120W PCIe:16x
ECC errors: 0
Processes: inference-service(3241) evicted (Xid 79)
Throttling: RT, Thermal, Pwr
```
```
dmesg | tail -n30
[ 12345.678] NVRM: Xid (0000:01:00): 79
[ 12345.679] kernel: i2c timeout on gpu fan sensor
[ 12346.000] watchdog: PSU rail B under-voltage detected: 11.7V
```
Alyssa: getting repeated "i2c timeout" and a PSU rail under-voltage message prior to the evictions
infra-bot: ALERT: cluster-monitor detected 3x GPU process evictions on gpu-eu-west1-rack8-12 in the last 45m. Added node to candidate-drain. (alert-id: cm-199876) :warning:
Matt: hm that nvidia-smi shows the power limit was enforced to 120W despite card capable of 250W — looks like a dynamic powercap step. could be PSU sag or BMC issuing cap. can you check BMC events?
Alyssa: grabbing BMC logs now, paste in a sec
Shreya: sounds like the "sawtooth" thermal pattern we've seen before where fans intermittently stop for a few seconds then full-spin, causing temp bursts and powercap fallback. but the PSU under-voltage is new. might be a failing PSU or a loose rail connection.
Alyssa: BMC snippet:
```
[09:11:02] PSU-B: Warning - Voltage sag 11.6V
[09:11:03] PMIC: Thermal trip cleared
[09:11:05] Fan 4: Tach lost pulses for 2s
[09:11:06] PSU-B: OCP reset
```
Kai: if the fan tach is dropping and PSU B is resetting that's a hardware-level transient. we should cordon the node and move inference traffic off it ASAP. can we do a fast drain and add a model fallback for 10m?
Matt: agree. Alyssa, run: `redwoodctl nodes drain gpu-eu-west1-rack8-12 --reason "psu/thermal transient" --timeout 15m` and then scale up a temporary replica in eu-west1-rack9 to absorb traffic. also set model routing policy to fallback to the smaller Llama-7b-quant during the drain.
Alyssa: running drain now. infra-bot: ACTION: Start drain for gpu-eu-west1-rack8-12 by Alyssa (timeout 15m). Moving 6 active inference jobs.
Kai: ops note — do not reboot the node yet. collect full i2c/fan telemetry and pmu logs, and attach to the ticket. repeated reboots can mask intermittent wiring/connector issues.
Shreya: if PSU-B is flapping we should schedule a hardware swap for that chassis. also recommend bumping fan curve to agressive for same-rack machines as a precaution (temporary).
Matt: quick triage checklist: 1) drain node and route traffic 2) collect nv-hostengine, BMC, dmesg, pmu logs 3) pin models off this node 4) open hw ticket (chassis/psu/fan) and request PSU swap + fan harness check 5) if repeats after swap, consider GPU RMA
Alyssa: logs uploaded to ticket INFRA-1428 with attached nv-hostengine and BMC dump. draining finished, jobs moved. latency normalized after routing to rack9.
infra-bot: NOTE: INFRA-1428 created and assigned to hardware-team. Estimated SLA contact within 2 business days.
Kai: after hardware swap, let's run a 24h soak with stress-ng + inference workload and telemetry enabled before returning node to production. also add a kpi monitor for short-lived fan tach losses so we catch this earlier.
Shreya: +1. also add an automated action: if PSU rail voltage < 11.8V and a fan tach lost pulse within 10s, auto-cordon node and page hw oncall. saves us from manual triage next time.
Alyssa: thanks all — keeping this thread updated with hw swap results. :thumbsup:
